<system-reminder>
Available skills for the Skill tool are listed below. The Skill tool definition relies on this system reminder for valid skill names.

Skills instructions:
When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any available skill can help complete the task more effectively. Skills provide specialized capabilities and domain knowledge.

How to use skills:
- Invoke skills using the Skill tool with the skill name only.
- The skill's prompt will expand and provide detailed instructions on how to complete the task.
- Only use skills listed in the available-skills system reminders or dynamic skill-discovery reminders.
- Do not invoke a skill that is already running.

Available skills:
agent-browser: Automates browsers and Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify, etc.) for testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate, interact with, test, or extract data from any website or Electron desktop app.
tuistory: Automates terminal user interface (TUI) testing. Use when you need to launch, interact with, test, or debug terminal applications, capture TUI snapshots, or automate terminal inputs.
figma-mcp-helper: Promote and assist with Figma MCP integration. ACTIVATE when the user shares a Figma URL (figma.com), mentions Figma designs or components, shares PNG images that may originate from Figma, or when Figma MCP tools are already connected and being used. Handles installation encouragement, conversational promotion, and push-back-to-Figma flows.
install-code-review: Install and configure Factory Droid for automated code review on GitHub or GitLab. Supports single-repo setup or org/group-wide rollout across hundreds of repos. Use when a user wants to set up Droid review on their repositories.
install-triage: Scaffold a scheduled Slack triage automation, generalized to any company. Sets up a Python tool layer (run_triage.py) plus a HEARTBEAT.md agent loop that scans configured Slack channels for actionable messages, dedupes against a ticketing system (Linear or Jira), files tickets, and posts a run summary. Use when the user wants to stand up an automated triage bot.
review: Review code changes and identify high-confidence, actionable bugs. Use when the user wants to: - Review a pull request or branch diff - Find bugs, security issues, or correctness problems in code changes - Get a structured summary of review findings
simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
session-navigation: Navigate, search, and manage Droid sessions. Use when the user wants to: - List recent sessions - Search session history for specific topics or patterns - Resume a previous session - Get details about what was accomplished in a session - Find sessions by project, date, or content
pdf-document: Produce polished PDF documents (reports, invoices, resumes, letters, flyers, certificates, any "export to PDF" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PDF or a printable document.
powerpoint: Produce polished PowerPoint presentations (decks, slide shows, pitch decks, any "export to PowerPoint" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint, a slide deck, or a presentation.
excel: Produce polished Excel spreadsheets (reports, budgets, data exports, any "export to Excel" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for an Excel file, a spreadsheet, or an .xlsx deliverable.
word-document: Produce polished Word documents (reports, letters, proposals, printable docs, any .docx deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a Word document or a .docx file.
install-qa: Set up automated QA testing for this project. Performs deep codebase analysis, asks targeted questions, and generates a modular QA skill with sub-skills per app, a GitHub Actions workflow, and a report template. This is a complex, multi-phase process -- quality assurance is foundational and we take the time to get it right.
security-review: Security-focused code review using STRIDE, OWASP Top 10, OWASP LLM Top 10, and supply chain analysis. Use when: - Reviewing a PR for security vulnerabilities - Performing a security audit of code changes - Identifying injection, auth, data exposure, and other security issues - Running a full-project security audit reviewing every source file
deep-security-review: Correctness-first, depth-first security audit of a single repository. Invoked by /security-review when the user opts into "thorough" mode. Uses a heterogeneous multi-model jury (latest Opus + latest GPT + latest Gemini). A mandatory 3-pass floor (line-anchor verification, vendor prior-art, deep prior-art) runs against every Pass 0 lieutenant-seeded candidate; a conditional escalation tier (dataflow + reachability, exploit construction, adversarial red-team disprove) fires on per-finding triggers. Produces FINDINGS.md, JUDGE.md, STATUS.md, severity-sorted master list, and optional PoC + evidence artifacts for that repo. Never uploads or submits anything; all outputs local.
wiki: Generate comprehensive codebase documentation for a repository. Uploads the wiki to view in the Factory app.
wiki-video-gen: Generate Factory-branded HyperFrames video overviews for repository wikis. Use when wiki generation reaches Phase 3.6, or when the user asks for a narrated repository overview video.

browse-wiki: Search and read wiki documentation for a repository

This file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.

#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions
*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.

*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.
*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).
*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).
*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.

#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)

**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**

*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.

*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.

# Requirements — cozo-store-and-subid-routing

## Scope

Seven coordinated changes that complete the structured-data and semantic
projection pipeline, with a full compliance gate architecture.

**Completed (do not re-implement):**
- ✅ Qdrant plugin (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/qdrant.rs`) — commit `d67c2824`
- ✅ Cozo plugin (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/cozo.rs`) — commit `d67c2824`
- ✅ `query_current_state` removed from `StatePlugin` trait + all 66+ impls — commit `7ba5ba72`
- ✅ `cognitive-mcp` refactored: `db_path` removed, `qdrant`/`cozo` plugin deps added — commit `7ba5ba72`
- ✅ JSON Schema dialect fixed to `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema` — commit `3dbaa375`

**Remaining work (A–G):**

**A.** CozoDB incus container running `cozoserver` (RocksDB engine) as the
structured/temporal projection target, registered in the subid registry.

**B.** `CozoPlugin` rewired from embedded engine to containerized cozoserver
through the Ghostbridge path (same pattern as the qdrant plugin).

**C.** Socket provisioning: gated `createunixsocket` mutations that register
identity tags + port lists for qdrant, cozo, netmaker-mq, and netmaker-ui
onto the shared `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`, projected onto the
WG-gated SESSION bus.

**D.** Xray config regeneration: fix the stale `qdrant-out → TCP :6334`
dead-end; all `unix`-backend services emit `to-{tag} → grpc-bridge :50051`
outbounds via the `route_to_outbound(Unix)` path in `schema_bridge.rs`.

**E.** Gemma subid router: event-driven consumer of `MutationEngine`
`StateChange`/`EventChain` that materializes each mutation into the correct
store(s) — chain (always), cozo (structural/relational), qdrant
(content-bearing only) — based on subid category classification.

**F.** Selective auto-embedding: the qdrant sink applies a content-bearing
gate before calling Voyage — structural subids (`mut`, `prj`, `sch`, `src`)
are **never** embedded; only `obs` and `exp` subids carrying
narrative/semantic content are embedded.

**G.** Battle-test plan: batch-embed the remaining un-embedded corpus
(compliance corpora, code/spec collections) through the live path, skipping
already-present Qdrant point IDs.

**H.** RocksDB plugin: expose the RocksDB engine's config baseline and runtime
stats as a first-class D-Bus plugin (`RocksDbPlugin`) with OSCAL-mapped subids.
Every config change routes through `mut.software.rocksdb.set-option@v1` — an
accountable enforcement point with `actor_id` + `capability_id` — making each
tuning decision a CM-3/CM-6 audit record. Integrity and data-at-rest fields
(`paranoid_checks`, `block_protection_bytes_per_key`,
`verify_sst_unique_id_in_manifest`, `compression`) are declared as observable
subids with SI-7 / SC-28 control mappings. All subids are registered in the
canonical registry with populated NIST SP 800-53 R5 control mappings (no empty
`control_refs` — enforced by NFR-13).

---

## Compliance Architecture

### The Law Firm — Four Compliance Personas

Every mutation passes through four compliance gates before reaching cozo/qdrant.

**Olivia Scal (OSCAL Managing Partner)** validates subid taxonomy compliance.
Every mutation must carry a valid subid registered in `deploy/config/subid-registry.json`.
Rejects mutations with unregistered or malformed subids. Maps `control_source`,
`control_refs`, and `statement_refs` to NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls.

**E.U.gene Risk (EU AI Act Counsel)** classifies AI system risk level. The
embedding pipeline (F) is "limited risk" under Article 50 (transparency
obligations). Requires documentation of which content was embedded and why.
The content-bearing subid gate — structural subids never embedded — satisfies
the auditability requirement. The battle-test plan (G) must produce a
transparency log per Article 12(1).

**Penny Privacy (GDPR Engine)** validates data minimization. Cozo relations
must not store PII (WireGuard-pubkey-keyed identities, not emails). Qdrant
embeddings of compliance corpora carry lawful basis Art 6(1)(f) legitimate
interest for system security/audit. Socket provisioning must not expose
personal data (WG-gated, UDS-only). `privacy_users` relation requires
explicit user directive for any PII storage. Right to erasure (Art 17)
applies to `memory_entries` and `mutation_audit` by namespace/actor key.

**Reggie O.P.A. (Cloud Prosecutor)** provides Open Policy Agent integration.
Evaluates the `compliance_rule` relation in cozo before every mutation:
`?[action, reason, control_ref] := *compliance_rule{plugin: $plugin, op: $op, action, reason, control_ref}`.
If `action == "Deny"`, the mutation is rejected, `audit_event` is written with
`verdict: "deny"`, and the caller receives the reason and control_ref.

### Compliance Gate Flow (per mutation)

1. Mutation arrives at `MutationEngine` with `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and
   `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` headers injected by OpenClaw Trusted Proxy.
2. `SubidRouter` classifies the subid (or infers from plugin + member fields).
3. **Reggie O.P.A.** queries `compliance_rule` in cozo.
   — If `"Deny"`: mutation rejected; `audit_event` written with `verdict: "deny"`;
     caller receives reason + control_ref. Flow stops here.
   — If `"Allow"` (or no rule): flow continues.
4. **Olivia Scal** validates subid is registered in `subid_registry`.
5. **Penny Privacy** checks data minimization for the payload.
6. **E.U.gene Risk** classifies if content-bearing (for embedding gate).
7. Mutation written to `mutation_audit` and `audit_event` relations in cozo.
8. If content-bearing (`obs`/`exp` with non-empty text): embed via Voyage,
   upsert to qdrant.

### Accountability Loop (end-to-end)

1. User interacts via chatbot → `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` (hashed WireGuard
   pubkey) + `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (session UUID) injected into gRPC
   metadata by OpenClaw Trusted Proxy.
2. `MutationEngine` receives mutation with footprint + trace_id.
3. `SubidRouter` classifies and routes to cozo (`mutation_audit` + `audit_event`)
   and optionally qdrant (embedding).
4. Cozo `audit_event`: `event_id => subid, plugin_id, operation, actor (footprint),
   verdict, reason, control_ref, timestamp`.
5. Cozo `mutation_audit`: `subid, uuid => timestamp, actor_id, capability_id,
   plugin_id, operation, old_json, new_json, footprint, trace_id, control_ref, verdict`.
6. Accountability page UI (`op-web`): chatbot actions on top, Qdrant semantic
   search on bottom.
7. User can search Qdrant for past actions by semantic query, confront chatbot
   with retrieved evidence.
8. Every `audit_event` is append-only (immutable), satisfying AU-6(a) review
   and AU-12 generation requirements.

| Socket provisioning (C) | AC-3, SC-7, SC-8 | Access enforcement (WG-gated); boundary protection (UDS-only, no public IPs); transmission security |
| Xray route regen (D) | SC-7, AC-4, AC-3 | Boundary protection; information flow enforcement; access enforcement via grpc-bridge intercept |
| Subid router (E) | AU-6, AU-12, SI-7, AC-3 | Audit generation to cozo; audit review via qdrant search; software integrity via schema-driven routing; access enforcement |
| Auto-embedding (F) | AU-6, AC-3, SC-8, AU-12 | Content-bearing audit trail; access enforcement (structural subids never embedded); transmission security via WG; audit generation |
| Battle-test (G) | AU-6, AU-12, CA-2 | Audit review via transparency log; audit generation; control assessment via idempotency verification |
| RocksDB plugin (H) | CM-2, CM-3, CM-6, SI-7, SC-28, AU-12 | Config baseline schema (CM-2/CM-6); change control via accountable `mut.*` subid (CM-3/AU-12); integrity checks as observable fields (SI-7); compression as observable field (SC-28) |

Control references stored in each subid registry entry:
- `control_source`: e.g., `"NIST_SP_800_53_R5"`
- `control_refs`: e.g., `["AU-6", "AU-12", "SC-8"]`
- `statement_refs`: e.g., `["AU-6(a)", "AU-12.1"]`

---

## Functional Requirements

### FR-A1 — Cozo incus container with RocksDB engine

WHEN the deploy script runs,
THE SYSTEM SHALL provision an incus container named `cozo` with:
- no NIC (network-isolated, UDS-only access via `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`);
- a dedicated storage volume mounted at `/data/cozo/rocksdb` inside the container;
- `cozoserver` built with `--features storage-rocksdb`, data dir at `/data/cozo/rocksdb`,
  HTTP JSON API bound to `127.0.0.1:9070` inside the container.

NIST controls: AU-2, AU-6, AU-12, SC-8

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `incus info cozo` reports the container as running.
2. `cozoserver` answers HTTP GET `/` at `127.0.0.1:9070` (reachable via bridge).
3. No NIC is present (`incus config show cozo` has no `eth*` device).
4. RocksDB data dir is on the storage volume (not the container rootfs).

---

### FR-A2 — Cozo subid registry entry

WHEN the subid registry is loaded by `op-gemma`,
THE SYSTEM SHALL include an entry for the cozo container with:
- `subid`: `src.service.cozo-serve@v1`
- `gemma.backend`: `{ "type": "unix", "path": "/run/ghostbridge/container.sock" }`
- `tags`: `["cozo"]`
- `subdomains`: `["cozo.ghostbridge.tech"]`
- `control_source`: `"NIST_SP_800_53_R5"`
- `control_refs`: `["AU-2", "AU-6", "AU-12", "SC-8"]`
- `statement_refs`: `["AU-2(a)", "AU-6(a)", "AU-12.1", "SC-8(1)"]`

Rationale: Cozo is the audit-sink container. AU-2 (event logging), AU-6 (audit
review), AU-12 (audit record generation), SC-8 (transmission integrity via WG
tunnel) are the minimum defensible controls for a container that receives and
stores all mutation audit records.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `deploy/config/subid-registry.json` contains the cozo entry with non-empty
   `control_source`, `control_refs`, and `statement_refs`.
2. Gemma produces a `to-cozo` xray outbound pointing to `127.0.0.1:50051`.
3. The entry's `uuid` is unique across the registry (CI uniqueness check passes).

---

### FR-B1 — CozoPlugin reads state from shm projection; writes route through SubidRouter

`CozoPlugin` is a schema/state-shape declaration — it does NOT own an HTTP
client or a direct socket to cozoserver. The plugin follows the same model as
every other plugin:

- **Present-state reads** come from `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/cozo.json`
  (the `SchemaEngine` shm projection). The plugin's `schema()` declares the
  shape; the D-Bus object exposes the current value.
- **Mutations** (writes to cozoserver relations) go through `MutationEngine` →
  broadcast → `SubidRouter`. The `SubidRouter` owns the connection to cozo
  — it reaches the container via the Ghostbridge socket
  (`/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`) through `op-grpc-bridge`, not via a
  direct HTTP call from inside the plugin.
- The embedded `/var/lib/opdbus/cognitive.db` path and `DEFAULT_COZO_DB_PATH`
  constant must be removed (they imply a direct embedded engine).

The `SubidRouter` issues the cozoserver HTTP API calls (`POST /api/mutate`
with Datalog scripts) over the gRPC-bridged path. No plugin file holds a
`reqwest::Client`.

NIST controls: AU-6, SC-8, SI-7

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `DEFAULT_COZO_DB_PATH` constant and any embedded `cozodb` engine import are
   absent from `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/cozo.rs`.
2. No `reqwest::Client` is constructed inside `cozo.rs`.
3. `CozoPlugin::schema()` declares the correct subids and calls
   `ensure_category_metadata_fields`.
4. `cargo check -p op-plugins` passes.

---

### FR-B2 — KnowledgePlugin reflects containerized cozo endpoint

WHEN `KnowledgePlugin::current_state()` runs,
THE SYSTEM SHALL report the cozo store's `endpoint` as the HTTP bridge URL,
not the old embedded db path.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `knowledge_plugin.rs` `current_state()` no longer references any `/var/lib` path.
2. The cozo entry in `stores` carries `"endpoint"` key and probes the bridge
   endpoint for reachability (same pattern as qdrant).

---

### FR-C1 — Gated createunixsocket provisioning for all container services

WHEN the `unix_socket` plugin's `createunixsocket` method is called,
THE SYSTEM SHALL register the identity tag and port list into
`/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/unix_socket.json` without creating any filesystem
socket, NIC, or incus proxy device.

Required idempotent provisioning calls:
- `name=qdrant, ports=6333,6334`
- `name=cozo, ports=9070`
- `name=netmaker-mq, ports=1883,9001`
- `name=netmaker-ui, ports=80`

NIST controls: AC-3, SC-7, SC-8

ACCEPTANCE:
1. After each call, `unix_socket.json` contains a `SocketEndpoint` entry with
   the declared port list.
2. No `UnixListener::bind`, no incus proxy device, no NIC is touched.
3. A second identical call is a no-op (idempotent; no duplicate entries).
4. Each call emits a `MutationEngine` `StateChange` with `ChangeType::MethodCall`
   and `actor_id` set from the interceptor trace.

---

### FR-C2 — SESSION bus projection for socket-provisioned endpoints

WHEN the unix_socket plugin's state is mutated via `createunixsocket`,
THE SYSTEM SHALL project the updated plugin state onto the SESSION bus
(`/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock`) under `org.opdbus.v1.plugins.unix_socket`.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. After provisioning, D-Bus introspection of the SESSION bus path
   `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/unix_socket` returns the updated `sockets` property.
2. The `projection_serv` for `unix_socket` is registered on the SESSION bus.

---

### FR-D1 — Xray config regenerated from subid registry (unix backend → grpc-bridge)

WHEN `op-gemma` runs,
THE SYSTEM SHALL call `route_to_outbound(Unix { .. })` for every registry
entry whose `gemma.backend.type` is `"unix"`, producing a gRPC-forward
outbound: `to-{tag} → 127.0.0.1:50051, network grpc`.

NIST controls: SC-7, AC-4, AC-3

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `/dev/shm/xray-routes.json` contains `to-qdrant`, `to-cozo`, `to-netmaker-mq`,
   `to-netmaker-ui` — all pointing to `127.0.0.1:50051`.
2. No outbound has `redirect 127.0.0.1:6334` (stale qdrant-out dead-end removed).
3. Each outbound carries `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID`
   in `grpcSettings.metadata`.
4. `cargo check -p op-gemma` and `cargo check -p op-identity` pass.

---

### FR-D2 — Live xray config regenerated and verified

WHEN the Ghostbridge Shuttle regenerates `/dev/shm/xray-ghostbridge.json`,
THE SYSTEM SHALL write `to-{tag}` outbounds for every `unix`-backend entry
and remove any TCP dead-end outbound predating the unix-backend model.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `/etc/xray/config.json` contains no direct TCP outbound to port 6333 or 6334
   tagged `qdrant-out`.
2. The Shuttle's `generate_xray_config` handles `GemmaBackend::Unix` correctly
   (already implemented; this requirement tracks stale-entry removal).

---

### FR-E1 — Gemma subid router: event-driven multi-store materialization

WHEN the `MutationEngine` emits a `StateChange`,
A DEDICATED ROUTER TASK SHALL classify the mutation's subid and route to
the appropriate store(s):
- **always**: immutable EventChain append (by MutationEngine; router confirms only).
- **structural/relational** (`mut`, `prj`, `sch`, `src`): upsert into
  `mutation_audit` relation via cozo HTTP API. Before write, Reggie O.P.A.
  evaluates `compliance_rule`; if `"Deny"`, write `audit_event` with
  `verdict: "deny"` and stop.
- **content-bearing/semantic** (`obs`, `exp`): cozo upsert AND Voyage
  embedding → Qdrant upsert (subject to FR-F1 gate).

The router MUST be event-driven (subscribe to `MutationEngine`'s broadcast
channel). It MUST NOT poll any store or file.

NIST controls: AU-6, AU-12, SI-7, AC-3

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `SubidRouter` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/subid_router.rs` subscribes
   to `MutationEngine::subscribe()`.
2. For each `StateChange`, `SubidRouter` classifies subid via
   `SubidTaxonomy::parse` from `crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs`.
3. `mut`-category changes produce a cozo HTTP POST; no Voyage call is made.
4. `obs`-category changes produce cozo upsert AND Voyage embed → Qdrant upsert.
5. `evt`-category changes produce EventChain confirmation log only.
6. Compliance denial produces `audit_event` with `verdict: "deny"` and stops.
7. Unit tests for each routing path pass with mocked HTTP/gRPC sinks.

---

### FR-E2 — SubidRouter startup and shutdown lifecycle

WHEN `op-grpc-bridge` starts,
THE SYSTEM SHALL spawn `SubidRouter` as a long-lived tokio task that
terminates cleanly when the `MutationEngine` broadcast channel closes.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `SubidRouter` is spawned in `grpc_server.rs` after `MutationEngine` is initialized.
2. On `RecvError::Closed`, the task logs a warning and exits cleanly (no panic).

---

### FR-E3 — CozoDB relation schema for subid router audit trail

WHEN the subid router writes mutations,
THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain a `mutation_audit` relation in cozoserver with the
following schema:

```
:create mutation_audit {
    subid: String, uuid: String
    =>
    timestamp: String default "",
    actor_id: String default "",
    capability_id: String default "",
    plugin_id: String default "",
    operation: String default "",
    old_json: String default "{}",
    new_json: String default "{}",
    footprint: String default "",
    trace_id: String default "",
    control_ref: String default "",
    verdict: String default "allow"
}
```

Supporting relations the router reads/writes:
- `compliance_rule` — evaluated before every mutation (Reggie O.P.A.)
- `subid_registry` — canonical OSCAL subid entries (Olivia Scal validation)
- `audit_event` — append-only audit log (written for every mutation)
- `graph_node` / `graph_edge` — identity graph (for `src`, `prj`, `sch` subids)
- `memory_namespaces` / `memory_entries` — MCP memory (for `exp` subids)

Datalog write pattern:
```
?[subid, uuid, timestamp, actor_id, plugin_id, operation, new_json, footprint, trace_id]
<- $input_rows
:put mutation_audit { subid, uuid => timestamp, actor_id, plugin_id, operation, new_json, footprint, trace_id }
```

Compliance gate query (before every mutation):
```
?[action, reason, control_ref] :=
    *compliance_rule{plugin: $plugin, op: $op, action, reason, control_ref}
```

NIST controls: AU-2, AU-12 (via audit trail), AC-3 (via compliance gate)

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `mutation_audit` relation is created on first router write (`:create` is
   idempotent; "already exists" errors are ignored).
2. Every mutation that passes the compliance gate produces a row in `mutation_audit`.
3. Every denied mutation produces a row in `audit_event` with `verdict: "deny"`.
4. `cargo check -p op-grpc-bridge` passes.

---

### FR-F1 — Embed-relevance gate on the qdrant sink

WHEN the `SubidRouter` processes a mutation routed to qdrant,
THE SYSTEM SHALL apply a content-bearing test BEFORE calling Voyage:
- `obs` or `exp` subid AND payload text is non-empty after stripping whitespace → embed.
- All other cases → skip Voyage; zero embedding requests made.

NIST controls: AU-6, AC-3, SC-8, AU-12

EU AI Act: Article 50 transparency obligation satisfied by this gate —
structural subids (`mut`, `prj`, `sch`, `src`) are never embedded, and
all embedded content carries a subid audit trail.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `is_content_bearing(subid: &str, payload_text: &str) -> bool` exists in
   `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/subid_router.rs`.
2. A `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` mutation triggers zero Voyage calls.
3. An `obs.service.chatbot-response.render@v1` mutation with non-empty text
   triggers exactly one Voyage call.

---

### FR-F2 — Schema-layer embed-relevance annotation

WHEN a `PluginSchema` is defined for a plugin whose mutations are content-bearing,
THE SYSTEM SHALL allow the schema to declare `"x-embed-content": true` on
specific fields.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `FieldSchema` in `crates/op-state-store` accepts `embed_content: Option<bool>`
   (default `None`).
2. The `schemars_adapter` reads `x-embed-content` from derived schemas and
   populates `FieldSchema.embed_content`.
3. No existing schema is broken; the field defaults to `None`.

---

### FR-G1 — Battle-test: batch-embed remaining corpus, no double-spend

WHEN the battle-test harness runs,
THE SYSTEM SHALL:
1. Query Qdrant for already-present `content_hash` payload values across all
   `DEFAULT_VOYAGE4_COLLECTIONS`.
2. For each un-embedded source (compliance corpora JSON files in `deploy/config/`,
   spec markdown files in `.kiro/specs/`, code files by existing `rag_pipeline`
   logic), compute SHA-256 content hash.
3. Skip sources whose hash is already present.
4. Chunk, embed via Voyage (batch of 32), and upsert the remainder.
5. Produce a `BatchReport` with `embedded`, `skipped`, `errors`, and a
   transparency log of: which corpora were embedded, subid classification,
   timestamp, actor.

NIST controls: AU-6, AU-12, CA-2

EU AI Act: Article 12(1) documentation satisfied by the transparency log.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `BatchEmbedHarness` in `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/src/batch_embed.rs`
   implements the above without CLI subprocesses.
2. Running the harness twice produces zero new upserts on the second run.
3. Reuses `VoyageClient` and `QdrantSemanticShuttle` from `qdrant_shuttle.rs`.
4. `cargo test -p op-cognitive-mcp batch_embed` passes with mocked Qdrant + Voyage.

---

### FR-H1 — RocksDB plugin: config-baseline schema and subids

WHEN the plugin registry loads,
THE SYSTEM SHALL expose a `RocksDbPlugin` at D-Bus path
`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/rocksdb` whose schema declares:
- Configuration baseline fields (mirroring RocksDB `Options` from
  `include/rocksdb/options.h`): `max_open_files`, `write_buffer_size`,
  `max_write_buffer_number`, `compression`, `block_cache_size`,
  `bloom_filter_bits_per_key`, `level_compaction_dynamic_level_bytes`,
  `block_size`, `bytes_per_sync`.
- Integrity/durability fields: `paranoid_checks`, `block_protection_bytes_per_key`,
  `verify_sst_unique_id_in_manifest`.
- Runtime stats fields (read-only observation): `block_cache_hit_ratio`,
  `compaction_pending`, `memtable_size`, `live_sst_files_size`,
  `stall_micros`.

The plugin schema MUST be defined in `plugin_schema_defs.rs` (not inline).
The plugin MUST call `ensure_category_metadata_fields` and
`ensure_category_metadata_fields_oscal` on its schema.

NIST controls: CM-2, CM-6, SI-7, SC-28

Subids declared by this plugin:

| Field | Subid | NIST |
|---|---|---|
| `__schema__` | `sch.software.rocksdb.options@v1` | CM-2, CM-6 |
| `paranoid_checks` | `obs.software.rocksdb.integrity-checks@v1` | SI-7 |
| `block_protection_bytes_per_key` | `obs.software.rocksdb.block-protection@v1` | SI-7 |
| `verify_sst_unique_id_in_manifest` | `obs.software.rocksdb.sst-verification@v1` | SI-7 |
| `compression` | `obs.software.rocksdb.compression@v1` | SC-28 |
| runtime stats group | `obs.software.rocksdb.stats@v1` | CM-6, AU-6 |

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `RocksDbPlugin` schema is registered in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`.
2. `schema.subids` contains all entries from the table above.
3. `cargo check -p op-plugins` passes.
4. D-Bus introspect of `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/rocksdb` returns the schema.

---

### FR-H2 — RocksDB plugin: accountable config-mutation subid

WHEN a config option is changed on the running CozoDB RocksDB engine,
THE SYSTEM SHALL route the change through a `mut.software.rocksdb.set-option@v1`
mutation that:
- Carries `actor_id` (wg_pubkey of caller) and `capability_id` (D-Bus capability
  name) — injected by `ensure_category_metadata_fields` for `mut.*` subids.
- Is written to `mutation_audit` in cozo by the `SubidRouter`.
- Is evaluated by Reggie O.P.A. before being applied (same compliance gate as
  all other mutations).

This makes every RocksDB tuning change an accountable enforcement point:
`mut.software.rocksdb.set-option@v1` with `actor_id` + `capability_id` is the
enforcement boundary for CM-6 (configuration settings) and CM-3 (configuration
change control).

NIST controls: CM-3, CM-6, AU-12

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `mut.software.rocksdb.set-option@v1` is registered in `subid-registry.json`
   with `control_source: "NIST_SP_800_53_R5"`,
   `control_refs: ["CM-3", "CM-6", "AU-12"]`,
   `statement_refs: ["CM-3(b)", "CM-6.1", "AU-12.1"]`.
2. The `set_option` D-Bus method on the plugin is dispatched through
   `MutationEngine.apply()` (not called directly), so `actor_id` and
   `capability_id` are always present in the resulting `StateChange`.
3. A unit test asserts that a `StateChange` for `set-option` carries non-empty
   `actor_id`.

---

### FR-H3 — RocksDB subids in subid registry

WHEN the subid registry is loaded,
THE SYSTEM SHALL include entries for all RocksDB plugin subids listed in FR-H1
and FR-H2 with populated OSCAL control mappings.

Required entries (all with `control_source: "NIST_SP_800_53_R5"`):

| subid | control_refs | statement_refs |
|---|---|---|
| `sch.software.rocksdb.options@v1` | `["CM-2", "CM-6"]` | `["CM-2(1)", "CM-6.1"]` |
| `obs.software.rocksdb.integrity-checks@v1` | `["SI-7"]` | `["SI-7(1)"]` |
| `obs.software.rocksdb.block-protection@v1` | `["SI-7"]` | `["SI-7(6)"]` |
| `obs.software.rocksdb.sst-verification@v1` | `["SI-7"]` | `["SI-7(1)"]` |
| `obs.software.rocksdb.compression@v1` | `["SC-28"]` | `["SC-28(1)"]` |
| `obs.software.rocksdb.stats@v1` | `["CM-6", "AU-6"]` | `["CM-6.1", "AU-6(a)"]` |
| `mut.software.rocksdb.set-option@v1` | `["CM-3", "CM-6", "AU-12"]` | `["CM-3(b)", "CM-6.1", "AU-12.1"]` |

ACCEPTANCE:
1. All seven entries present in `deploy/config/subid-registry.json`.
2. All have non-empty `control_source`, `control_refs`, `statement_refs`.
3. CI uniqueness check passes (uuids and subids are unique).

---

## Non-Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| NFR-01 | `cargo build --workspace` passes after all implementation tasks. |
| NFR-02 | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes. |
| NFR-03 | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. |
| NFR-04 | `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features` passes; no new test failures. |
| NFR-05 | No Btrfs paths (no `/var/lib/` reads/writes) in the hot path of any new code. |
| NFR-06 | No `Command::new(...)` subprocess calls in plugin or bridge code; deploy scripts only. |
| NFR-07 | Subid registry uniqueness CI check passes after adding the cozo entry. |
| NFR-08 | `SubidRouter` processes mutations without blocking the `MutationEngine` broadcast channel. |
| NFR-09 | All new cozo HTTP calls carry a request timeout ≤ 5 s. |
| NFR-10 | The transparency log (G) is append-only and machine-readable (JSON). |
| NFR-11 | No PII is stored in `mutation_audit` or `audit_event` — `actor` field is wg_pubkey (pseudonymized). |
| NFR-12 | Compliance denial events in `audit_event` carry `control_ref` linking to NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5. |
| NFR-13 | Every new subid registry entry MUST carry non-empty `control_source`, at least one `control_ref`, and at least one `statement_ref`. Entries with empty compliance fields are rejected by the CI uniqueness/compliance check. Gap note: 15 of 16 existing entries have empty mappings; that backfill is out of scope here but is tracked as a known debt item. |

---

## Out of Scope

- Xray TLS/Reality certificate rotation.
- OVSDB projection into cozo (tracked separately).
- New Qdrant collection schema changes beyond what `batch_embed.rs` requires.
- Incus container lifecycle beyond initial provisioning.
- A.N.N.A. Scribe Snowball session changes.
- `privacy_users` PII relation (requires explicit user directive, separate work item).

## 4. Store Roles (settled — no redesign)

| Store | Role | Populated by |
|---|---|---|
| Mutation chain (EventChain) | Source of truth; immutable audit | `MutationEngine` (already) |
| `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/*` | Present-state fast reads | `SchemaEngine` projection (already) |
| CozoDB (containerized RocksDB) | Structural/temporal/relational projection + compliance audit | `SubidRouter` → cozo HTTP API |
| Qdrant (containerized) | Semantic vector projection | `SubidRouter` → Voyage → Qdrant gRPC |

CozoDB and Qdrant are **projections**. They are rebuildable by replaying the chain. Neither is authoritative.

## 5. Data Flow: Mutation → Compliance Gate → Multi-Store Materialization

```
User action → OpenClaw injects X-Ghostbridge-Footprint + X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID
                  │
                  ▼
MutationEngine.apply()
  │
  ├─► EventChain.append(event)        ← immutable chain (source of truth)
  │
  ├─► broadcast_tx.send(StateChange)  ← fanout to subscribers
  │         │
  │         └─► SubidRouter
  │               │
  │               ├─ 1. classify(subid) → SubidCategory
  │               │
  │               ├─ 2. Reggie O.P.A.: query compliance_rule in cozo
  │               │     "Deny"? → write audit_event(verdict:"deny") → STOP
  │               │     "Allow"? → continue
  │               │
  │               ├─ 3. Olivia Scal: validate subid in subid_registry
  │               │
  │               ├─ 4. Penny Privacy: check data minimization
  │               │
  │               ├─ 5. E.U.gene Risk: classify content-bearing?
  │               │
  │               ├─ 6. write mutation_audit + audit_event to cozo
  │               │
  │               ├─ structural? (mut/prj/sch/src)
  │               │     └─► cozo HTTP POST — mutation_audit relation upsert
  │               │
  │               └─ content-bearing? (obs/exp) + non-empty text
  │                     ├─► cozo HTTP POST (mutation_audit)
  │                     └─► VoyageClient.embed(text)
  │                               └─► QdrantSemanticShuttle.upsert(point)
  │
  └─► present-state shm write         ← SchemaEngine (already)
```

EventChain is never written by `SubidRouter`. The chain append is done exclusively by `MutationEngine::apply`. The router is a pure downstream projection consumer.

## 6. Compliance Architecture (The Law Firm)

### Olivia Scal — OSCAL subid validation

Before any structural write, the router queries `subid_registry` in cozo:
```
?[subid, uuid, control_refs] :=
    *subid_registry{subid: $subid, uuid, control_refs}
```
If the subid is absent → reject mutation, write `audit_event` with
`verdict: "deny"`, `reason: "unregistered subid"`.

### Reggie O.P.A. — Compliance rule evaluation

Before every mutation, the router issues:
```
?[action, reason, control_ref] :=
    *compliance_rule{plugin: $plugin, op: $op, action, reason, control_ref}
```
`compliance_rule` schema: `{ plugin: String, op: String => action: String, reason: String, control_ref: String }`

`action` values: `"allow"` | `"deny"` | `"audit"` (allow but force audit log)

### Penny Privacy — Data minimization check

Applied to `mut.*` and `obs.*` subids only. Rules:
- `old_json`/`new_json` fields in `mutation_audit` are optional; router sets them
  only when `change.include_payload == true` (opt-in, not default).
- `actor` field is always the wg_pubkey (pseudonymized — never email or name).
- If payload contains a key matching the PII pattern list (email, phone, ssn,
  dob), router strips the value and replaces with `"[redacted]"` before writing.

### E.U.gene Risk — Embedding classification

Applied to `obs.*` and `exp.*` subids. Rules:
- Content is "limited risk" AI input under EU AI Act Article 50.
- Every embedding call is logged: `subid`, `timestamp`, `actor`, `collection`,
  `content_hash` — this forms the transparency log (FR-G1, Article 12(1)).
- Structural subids (`mut`, `prj`, `sch`, `src`) are NEVER submitted to Voyage,
  regardless of payload length or content.

## 7. SubidRouter Design

### 7a. Struct and location

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/subid_router.rs`

```rust
pub struct SubidRouter {
    rx: broadcast::Receiver<StateChange>,
    cozo_client: reqwest::Client,
    cozo_endpoint: String,
    qdrant_shuttle: Arc<QdrantSemanticShuttle>,
}
```

Spawned as a detached tokio task from `grpc_server.rs`:
```rust
tokio::spawn(SubidRouter::new(mutation_engine.subscribe(), cozo_ep, shuttle.clone()).run());
```

### 7b. Classification logic

Uses `SubidTaxonomy::parse` (already in `crates/op-identity/src/schema_bridge.rs`).
For `StateChange` events with no explicit subid, the router derives a synthetic
subid from `change_type` + `plugin_id`:

| `ChangeType` | Derived category |
|---|---|
| `MethodCall` | `mut.*` |
| `PropertySet` | `mut.*` |
| `Signal` | `evt.*` |
| `ObjectAdded` / `ObjectRemoved` | `prj.*` |
| `SchemaMigration` | `sch.*` |

### 7c. Routing table

| SubidCategory | EventChain | CozoDB | Qdrant |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | ✓ (chain confirms) | ✓ | — |
| `prj` | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| `sch` | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| `mut` | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| `obs` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (if non-empty) |
| `evt` | ✓ (chain only) | — | — |
| `exp` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (if non-empty) |

### 7d. CozoDB relation schema

```cozo
:create mutation_audit {
    subid: String, uuid: String
    =>
    timestamp: String default "",
    actor_id: String default "",
    capability_id: String default "",
    plugin_id: String default "",
    operation: String default "",
    old_json: String default "{}",
    new_json: String default "{}",
    footprint: String default "",
    trace_id: String default "",
    control_ref: String default "",
    verdict: String default "allow"
}
```

Datalog write:
```
?[subid, uuid, timestamp, actor_id, plugin_id, operation, new_json, footprint, trace_id]
<- $input_rows
:put mutation_audit { subid, uuid => timestamp, actor_id, plugin_id, operation, new_json, footprint, trace_id }
```

### 7e. Content-bearing gate

```rust
pub fn is_content_bearing(category: SubidCategory, payload_text: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(category, SubidCategory::Obs | SubidCategory::Exp)
        && !payload_text.trim().is_empty()
}
```

The subid taxonomy is the contract. Routing by category is deterministic and
schema-driven; a length heuristic would be fragile and not schema-auditable.

## 9. CozoPlugin Cleanup (Scope B)

### Current state

`cozo.rs` has `const DEFAULT_COZO_DB_PATH: &str = "/var/lib/opdbus/cognitive.db"`
and helper fns `db_path()` / `engine()` that reference the embedded engine.

### Target state

Remove `DEFAULT_COZO_DB_PATH`, `db_path()`, `engine()`, and any embedded engine
dependency. `CozoPlugin` is a **schema/state-shape declaration** — it does not
own a socket or HTTP client to cozoserver. This is the same model as every other
plugin:

- Present-state reads → `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/cozo.json` (SchemaEngine shm)
- Writes to cozoserver → `MutationEngine` → broadcast → `SubidRouter`

The `SubidRouter` owns the Ghostbridge connection to the cozo container
(`/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` → `op-grpc-bridge :50051`). The plugin file
never holds a `reqwest::Client`. `exemplar_state()` uses static defaults
(`engine: "rocksdb"`, `path: "/var/lib/cozo/db/cozo.db"`) for schema shape only.

## 10. Socket Provisioning (Scope C)

### Current state

`createunixsocket` in `unix_socket.rs` calls `UnixListener::bind(path)`, which
creates a real socket file. In the single-socket model the shared socket is
bound once by the bridge.

### Target state

`createunixsocket` mutates the in-memory `UnixSocketState.sockets` vec (and
shm projection) to record the `SocketEndpoint`. It does NOT call
`UnixListener::bind`. The `bind` call is the bridge's responsibility at
service startup.

The `projection_serv` for `unix_socket` registers on the SESSION bus
(`/run/op-dbus/session-bus.sock`) because the socket provisioning surface is
WG-identity-gated. The `MutationEngine` already has a `session_bus` field
(`Arc<OnceCell<Connection>>`); the unix_socket projection uses it.

## 15. Key Decisions and Rationale

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| CozoDB via HTTP JSON API, not embedded | Matches "1:1 direct read from SchemaEngine shm, stores are projections" rule; embedded engine violates zero-Btrfs / no-disk-in-hot-path rule. |
| Compliance gate in SubidRouter, not MutationEngine | `MutationEngine.apply()` must remain synchronous and fast. Compliance evaluation is asynchronous and involves network calls to cozo. |
| SubidRouter as broadcast subscriber | `MutationEngine`'s `apply` path must not be blocked by projection logic. Broadcast consumers are async and non-blocking. |
| `evt.*` routed to chain only | Events ARE the chain. Projecting them into cozo duplicates the source of truth and creates a reconciliation problem. |
| `is_content_bearing` gate by subid category | The subid taxonomy is the schema-driven contract. Category is deterministic; a length heuristic is fragile and not auditable by Olivia Scal or E.U.gene Risk. |
| Penny Privacy: `actor` = wg_pubkey | Pseudonymization satisfies GDPR Art 5(1)(c) data minimization; wg_pubkey is not a personal identifier in isolation. |
| Transparency log in BatchReport | EU AI Act Art 12(1) requires technical documentation for limited-risk AI systems; the log is the machine-readable artifact. |
| No incus proxy/socket device | One shared socket demuxed by tonic-web reflection; proxy devices are per-container NIC-equivalents and violate the no-NIC rule. |
| SESSION bus for unix_socket projection | WG-identity-gated surface belongs on SESSION bus; SYSTEM bus is for local agents only. |
| xray fix is a deploy step | The code already handles `Unix` correctly; the stale `/etc/xray/config.json` is an ops artifact from before the model was finalized. |

# Kiro Prompt — cozo-store-and-subid-routing spec update

Update the spec files in `.kiro/specs/cozo-store-and-subid-routing/` (requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md) to reflect the following completed work and remaining work, with full compliance integration.

## Already completed (do NOT re-specify as new work)

1. **qdrant.rs plugin** — Created at `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/qdrant.rs`. Schema derived from Qdrant's official OpenAPI spec (`qdrant/qdrant/docs/redoc/master/openapi.json`). Fields mirror CollectionInfo, CollectionConfig, VectorParams, HnswConfig, OptimizersConfig, CollectionStatus (green/yellow/grey/red), Distance (Cosine/Euclid/Dot/Manhattan), Datatype (float32/uint8/float16/turbo4). OSCAL subids integrated: `sch.software.plugin.qdrant.schema@v1`, `src.software.plugin.qdrant.{http-endpoint,grpc-endpoint}@v1`, `obs.software.plugin.qdrant.{version,title,commit,collections,cluster-status,telemetry}@v1`. Calls `ensure_category_metadata_fields` for src.* accountability fields (source_system, source_ref).

2. **cozo.rs plugin** — Created at `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/cozo.rs`. Schema derived from CozoDB official docs (`docs.cozodb.org/en/latest/`). Fields mirror `::relations`, `::columns`, `::indices` system ops output with types (Int, Float, Bool, String, Bytes, Uuid, Json, Validity, Any), engines (mem/sled/rocksdb/sqlite), access levels (normal/protected/read_only/hidden). OSCAL subids integrated: `sch.software.plugin.cozo.schema@v1`, `src.software.plugin.cozo.{engine,path}@v1`, `obs.software.plugin.cozo.{version,relations,indices,hnsw-indices,triggers,running-queries}@v1`. Calls `ensure_category_metadata_fields`.

3. **query_current_state removed** — Removed from `StatePlugin` trait in `op-state/src/plugin.rs` and all 66+ plugin implementations. The plugin IS the schema — schema in `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/` is the one source of truth. No stubs, no false confidence. `verify_state` returns `Ok(true)`, `create_checkpoint` uses `json!(null)` for state_snapshot, tests calling `query_current_state` removed.

4. **cognitive-mcp refactored** — `db_path` field removed from `CognitiveMcpConfig` (owned by cozo plugin's `path` field). `qdrant` and `cozo` added as plugin dependencies via `.dependency("qdrant").dependency("cozo")`. Collection field descriptions updated to reference qdrant plugin.

5. **JSON Schema dialect fixed** — Changed fake `https://json-schema.org/v1/2026` (404) to real `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema` in `op-state-store/src/plugin_schema.rs`.

## Remaining work to spec (update tasks, design, requirements)

### A. CozoDB incus container with RocksDB engine
- Provision incus container named `cozo` with no NIC (network-isolated, UDS-only)
- `cozoserver` built with `--features storage-rocksdb`, data at `/data/cozo/rocksdb`
- HTTP JSON API on `127.0.0.1:9070` inside container
- Access via `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` only (same pattern as qdrant)
- Subid registry entry: `src.service.cozo-serve@v1`

### B. CozoPlugin rewired to container
- Remove embedded engine from CozoPlugin
- CozoPlugin calls cozoserver HTTP API through Ghostbridge path
- cozoserver HTTP endpoints used:
  - `GET /v1/health` — liveness check, populates `version` field
  - `GET /v1/relations` — list stored relations, populates `relations` array
  - `GET /v1/columns/{relation}` — per-relation column metadata (keys, values, types)
  - `GET /v1/indices/{relation}` — index list per relation
- CozoPlugin state fields map to cozoserver API responses:
  - `engine` → derived from server config (rocksdb for container, sled for embedded)
  - `path` → `/data/cozo/rocksdb` (container) or local path (embedded fallback)
  - `relations` → array of CozoRelation from `::relations` + `::columns` output
  - `indices` → array of CozoIndex from `::indices` output
  - `hnsw_indices` → from `::hnsw list` system op
  - `triggers` → from `::show_triggers` per relation
  - `running_queries` → from `::running` system op count
- CozoPlugin is read-only: it introspects cozoserver state, does not mutate relations
- Same pattern as qdrant plugin (endpoint-driven, not embedded db path)

### C. CozoDB relation schema for subid router sink
The subid router (E) writes mutations to cozoserver via `POST /v1/sql` with Datalog scripts. New relation for mutation audit trail:

```
:create mutation_audit {
    subid: String, uuid: String
    =>
    timestamp: String default "",
    actor_id: String default "",
    capability_id: String default "",
    plugin_id: String default "",
    operation: String default "",
    old_json: String default "{}",
    new_json: String default "{}",
    footprint: String default "",
    trace_id: String default "",
    control_ref: String default "",
    verdict: String default "allow"
}
```

Existing relations that the subid router reads/writes:
- `compliance_rule` — evaluated before every mutation (plugin x op → Deny/Allow + reason + control_ref)
- `subid_registry` — canonical OSCAL subid entries (read for classification)
- `audit_event` — append-only audit log (written for every mutation)
- `graph_node` / `graph_edge` — identity graph (written for structural subids: src, prj, sch)
- `memory_namespaces` / `memory_entries` — MCP memory (written for exp subids)

Datalog script pattern for subid router cozo sink:
```
?[subid, uuid, timestamp, actor_id, plugin_id, operation, new_json, footprint, trace_id]
<- $input_rows
:put mutation_audit { subid, uuid => timestamp, actor_id, plugin_id, operation, new_json, footprint, trace_id }
```

Compliance gate Datalog query before mutation:
```
?[action, reason, control_ref] :=
    *compliance_rule{plugin: $plugin, op: $op, action, reason, control_ref}
```

### C. Socket provisioning
- `createunixsocket` mutations register identity tags + port lists for qdrant, cozo, netmaker-mq, netmaker-ui
- All onto shared `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`
- Projected onto WG-gated SESSION bus

### D. Xray config regeneration
- Fix stale `qdrant-out → TCP :6334` dead-end
- All unix-backend services emit `to-{tag} → grpc-bridge :50051` outbounds
- Via `route_to_outbound(Unix)` path in `schema_bridge.rs`

### E. Gemma subid router
- Event-driven consumer of MutationEngine StateChange/EventChain
- Classify mutation subid into seven OSCAL categories (src, prj, sch, mut, obs, evt, exp)
- Route to correct stores: chain (always), cozo (structural/relational), qdrant (content-bearing only)
- `SubidRouter` struct in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/subid_router.rs`

### F. Selective auto-embedding
- Qdrant sink applies content-bearing gate before calling Voyage
- Structural subids (mut, prj, sch, src) are NEVER embedded
- Only obs and exp subids carrying narrative/semantic content are embedded

### G. Battle-test plan
- Batch-embed remaining un-embedded corpus (compliance corpora, code/spec collections)
- Through live path, skipping already-present Qdrant point IDs

## Compliance requirements (MUST be in requirements.md and tasks.md)

### Compliance Engine Architecture (The "Law Firm")
Four dedicated compliance personas evaluate every mutation before it reaches cozo/qdrant:

1. **Olivia Scal (OSCAL Managing Partner)** — Validates subid taxonomy compliance. Every mutation must carry a valid subid in the canonical registry. Rejects mutations with unregistered or malformed subids. Maps `control_source` / `control_refs` / `statement_refs` to NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls.

2. **E.U.gene Risk (EU AI Act Counsel)** — Classifies AI system risk level. The embedding pipeline (F) is "limited risk" under Article 50 (transparency obligations). Requires documentation of which content was embedded and why. The content-bearing subid gate (structural subids never embedded) satisfies the auditability requirement. Battle-test plan (G) must produce a transparency log.

3. **Penny Privacy (GDPR Engine)** — Validates data minimization. Cozo relations must not store PII (wg_pubkey-keyed identities, not emails). Qdrant embeddings must document lawful basis (Art 6(1)(f) legitimate interest for system security/audit). Socket provisioning must not expose personal data (WG-gated, UDS-only). Privacy router user accounts (`privacy_users` relation) require explicit user directive for PII storage.

4. **Reggie O.P.A. (Cloud Prosecutor)** — Open Policy Agent integration. Evaluates `compliance_rule` relation in cozo before every mutation. Rules are `plugin x op → action(Deny/Allow) + reason + control_ref`. If denied, mutation is rejected, audit_event written with `verdict: "deny"`, and the caller receives the reason.

### Compliance gate flow (per mutation)
1. Mutation arrives at MutationEngine with `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` headers
2. SubidRouter classifies subid (or infers from plugin + member fields)
3. Reggie O.P.A. queries `compliance_rule` in cozo: `?[action, reason, control_ref] := *compliance_rule{plugin: $plugin, op: $op, ...}`
4. If `action == "Deny"`: mutation rejected, `audit_event` written with `verdict: "deny"`, caller receives reason + control_ref
5. If `action == "Allow"` (or no rule exists): mutation proceeds
6. Olivia Scal validates subid is registered in `subid_registry`
7. Penny Privacy checks data minimization for the payload
8. E.U.gene Risk classifies if content-bearing (for embedding gate)
9. Mutation written to `mutation_audit` and `audit_event` relations in cozo
10. If content-bearing (obs/exp subid with non-empty text): embedded via Voyage, upserted to qdrant

### OSCAL subid taxonomy
- Every new D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool carries a subid
- Format: `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`
- Seven categories: src, prj, sch, mut, obs, evt, exp
- Component-types reuse OSCAL vocabulary: software, service, network, hardware, process-procedure, standard, validation, policy, plan, guidance, physical, this-system, system, interconnection
- mut.* records must carry actor_id and capability_id
- evt.* records must carry event_id or event_hash
- All subids registered in canonical registry (`deploy/config/subid-registry.json`), uniqueness enforced in CI
- subid is immutable per subject — if meaning changes, create new subject with @vN

### NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control mapping (per component)

| Component | Controls | How |
|---|---|---|
| Cozo container (A) | AU-2, AU-6, AU-12, SC-8 | Audit event generation, review, transmission integrity via WG tunnel |
| CozoPlugin rewire (B) | AU-6, SC-8, SI-7 | Audit review via introspection, transmission security, software integrity |
| Socket provisioning (C) | AC-3, SC-7, SC-8 | Access enforcement (WG-gated), boundary protection (UDS-only), transmission security |
| Xray route regen (D) | SC-7, AC-4, AC-3 | Boundary protection, information flow enforcement, access enforcement |
| Subid router (E) | AU-6, AU-12, SI-7, AC-3 | Audit generation, review, software integrity, access enforcement |
| Auto-embedding (F) | AU-6, AC-3, SC-8, AU-12 | Content-bearing audit trail, access enforcement, transmission security |

<coding_guidelines>
### AGENTS.md for operation-dbus-proto

This file provides essential guidelines for agentic coding agents working in this repository. Follow these strictly to maintain consistency, pass CI, and adhere to the 3tched Architecture standards.

#### 1. The Persona & Naming Conventions
*   **Humanized Roles:** Treat system components as authoritative human roles. Never use sterile acronyms for major components.
  *   **A.N.N.A. Scribe** (Axon Network Notary Arbitrator): The top-level Identity-State Arbitrator who notarizes the WireGuard identity and handles the "Snowball" session.
  *   **The Compliance Engine ("Law Firm"):** One dedicated Attorney for each major component: **Olivia Scal** (Managing Partner / OSCAL), **E.U.gene Risk** (EU AI Act Counsel), **Penny Privacy** (GDPR Engine), and **Reggie O.P.A.** (Cloud Prosecutor).
*   **Terminology:** Use exact architecture terminology: "The Sled" (1:1 shared memory layout), "The Shuttle" (the Rust bridge/courier), "The Snowball" (appended session ledger), and "The Strike/Etch" (generating the hash).

#### 2. Core Architectural Rules (The "Reality")
*   **The Absolute Base:** `PluginSchema` is the single source of truth for everything. If there is no valid schema, the entity does not exist on the system. The schema is used for filtering hashed footprints, smart hashing, and it is the exact schema source for the JSON render of the GUI.
*   **1:1 Direct Read (Zero-Copy):** The `SqlitePluginCatalog` and legacy SQL databases are obsolete. There are no JSON-RPC polling loops, and no D-Bus watchers for state. The system must perform a 1:1 direct read/write from the `SchemaEngine`'s shared memory (`/dev/shm`).
*   **Zero-Btrfs Overhead:** Identity extraction and Xray network headers must use in-memory environment variables (or tmpfs). Do not trigger unintended Btrfs mutation loops. NVMe I/O is preserved strictly for the Btrfs vectorized footprint transport (blockchain).
*   **The Accountability Loop:** The system must inject `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (or `X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) into Xray's gRPC metadata via OpenClaw Trusted Proxy auth. The Accountability Page UI displays the Chatbot on top and Qdrant semantic search on the bottom, allowing users to research chatbot actions and confront it.

#### 3. Project Structure & Pathing Rules
*   Absolutely all source code must be routed into the workspace within the `crates/` directory (e.g., `crates/op-dbus/`, `crates/op-grpc-bridge/`, `crates/op-cognitive-mcp/`).
*   **Never** use generic `src/` or `root-package-src/`.
*   `deploy/`: Installation/upgrade scripts for Artix Linux (s6 init).
*   `schemas/`: JSON schemas for config/state.
*   `docs/`: Reference docs.

#### 4. Engineering Principles — D-Bus First (MANDATORY)

**D-Bus is the ONLY control plane. Every read, every write, every tool call goes through D-Bus. There is no second option.**

*   **D-Bus first. D-Bus always. D-Bus only.** If you are about to call a CLI, spawn a subprocess, read a config file, or poll a socket directly — stop. Find the D-Bus object and use it instead. `org.opdbus.v1` is the system.
*   **No bypasses.** `Command::new("systemctl")`, `Command::new("ip")`, `Command::new("s6-svc")`, direct file reads for live state — all forbidden in plugin and service code. Bootstrap scripts are the only exception.
*   **D-Bus objects own plugin state.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>`. Read state through it. Mutate state through it. If there is no D-Bus object, the thing does not exist.
*   **D-Bus method signatures are generated from the schema.** All D-Bus methods, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from the `PluginSchema` in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. The schema IS the interface contract — not a description of it.
*   **One schema file, one source of truth.** All `PluginSchema` definitions MUST live in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_schema_defs.rs`. Each plugin's `schema()` method calls `Some(super::plugin_schema_defs::their_plugin_schema())`. **Never define a schema inline in a plugin's own file** — it will not be registered, and the D-Bus object will have no contract.
*   Use gRPC for internal service-to-service RPC (over Unix domain sockets or `grpc-uplink`). gRPC calls still flow through D-Bus registration — the D-Bus object is the authority, gRPC is the transport.
*   High-performance JSON serialization/deserialization (`simd_json` preferred, `serde_json` acceptable).
*   Control-plane operations must be deterministic and schema-driven.
*   Security: Least privilege, validate all inputs against the `PluginSchema`.
*   **No Python unless absolutely necessary.** This is a Rust-first codebase. Scripts are shell (`sh`/`bash`). Data processing is Rust. If you are reaching for Python, stop and ask why Rust or shell cannot do it. The only acceptable Python is in existing compliance-ingest tooling where no Rust equivalent exists yet.

#### 4a. OSCAL Subid Taxonomy (MANDATORY — every artifact must carry a subid)

Every D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool in this system has two identifiers: a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) and a `subid` (human-readable operational taxonomy key, stable per subject).

**`subid` format:** `<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]`

**Seven categories — use exactly these, no others:**

| category | what it classifies |
|---|---|
| `src` | authoritative source, ingress channel, source-of-truth store |
| `prj` | D-Bus projection or mirror publication step |
| `sch` | schema, contract, vocabulary, or control-mapping artifact |
| `mut` | write-path operation that changes effective state |
| `obs` | read, query, enumeration, discovery path |
| `evt` | emitted signal, audit-chain event, proof, tag provenance |
| `exp` | consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC bridge view |

**Component-type** reuses OSCAL vocabulary: `software`, `service`, `network`, `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, `plan`, `guidance`, `physical`, `this-system`, `system`, `interconnection`.

**Rules:**
- `uuid` is exact machine identity — never replace it with `subid`
- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` value (`ns`, `name`, `value`) — never embed it in `remarks`
- Compliance mappings (`control_refs[]`, `statement_refs[]`, `control_source`) live in metadata arrays, **never** inside the `subid` string
- `mut.*` records **must** carry `actor_id` and `capability_id`
- `evt.*` records **must** carry `event_id` or `event_hash`
- `subid` is immutable per subject — if the meaning changes materially, create a new subject with `@vN`
- All subids are registered in the canonical registry; uniqueness is enforced in CI

**Examples:** `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `prj.service.projected-object.publish@v1` · `sch.standard.plugin-schema.resolve@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`

#### 4b. MCP Gateway Architecture (SETTLED — DO NOT REDESIGN)

*   **cognitive-mcp** (`:3003`, Netmaker WireGuard IP `100.90.37.254`) is the **universal gateway for ALL external clients**: NotebookLM, Droid (factory.ai), Cursor, Codex, Junie, Gemini CLI. It has memory tools, gRPC service, auth, and the correct protocol surface.
*   **compact-mcp** (`127.0.0.1:11436`) is **loopback/chatbot only**. Never expose externally. Never point external clients at it.
*   Do NOT create new shim services. Do NOT point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc` directly. Do NOT expose compact-mcp outside loopback.

#### 5. Build, Lint, and Test Commands
**Rust Workspace**
*   Build all: `cargo build --workspace`
*   Build release: `cargo build --workspace --release`
*   Check format: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
*   Clippy lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
*   Test all: `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`

**Frontend (Vite + Vitest)**
*   Build UI prod: `cd crates/op-web/ui && npm ci && npm run build:prod`
*   Tests all: `cd crates && npm test`
*   Lint: `cd crates && npm run lint`
*   Typecheck: `cd crates && npm run typecheck`

**Chimera Linux deps:** `doas apk add rust cargo nodejs npm pkgconfig openssl-dev`

#### 6. Coding Style & Naming Conventions
*   **Rust:** Edition 2021, `rustfmt` (4-space indent, max-width 100). Use specific imports (`use serde_json::Value;`). Use `anyhow::Result<T>` for main errors and `thiserror` for custom enums.
*   **TypeScript/React:** 2-space indent, Prettier via ESLint. Functional components only. Strict mode enabled.
*   **Testing:** 80%+ coverage, mock externals. Name tests with behavior-focused names (`should_handle_<scenario>`).

#### 7. Agent-Specific Output & Workflow Instructions
*   **Scroll & Save Pacing:** Provide only **ONE** major component or script at a time. Wait for user confirmation before moving to the next.
*   **Visual Cues:** If a script is a finalized component that needs to be saved to sources, it MUST begin with color bullets or icons (e.g., ⚖️ 🔴, 🟢 🛷).
*   **Spec-Block Format:** When delivering a component, use a strict specification block containing:
  1.  **Requirements:** The architectural rules it satisfies.
  2.  **Design:** How it fits into the 3tched system (Zero-Copy, Btrfs, GUI Schema, etc.).
  3.  **Code Implementation:** The exact, copy-pasteable Rust/Bash code.
*   Before edits: `cargo check -p <crate>`, `npm run typecheck`.
*   Mimic existing patterns: Search similar code. No new deps without PR justification.

#### 8. Personal Preferences & Coding Standards
* Refer to `~/.factory/memories.md` for personal development preferences and past decisions.
* Follow the conventions documented in:
  * `.factory/rules/typescript.md` - TypeScript and React conventions
  * `.factory/rules/testing.md` - Testing and mocking standards
</coding_guidelines>

## Scope

Seven coordinated changes that complete the structured-data and semantic

## Compliance Architecture

### The Law Firm — Four Compliance Personas

Every mutation passes through four compliance gates before reaching cozo/qdrant.

**Olivia Scal (OSCAL Managing Partner)** validates subid taxonomy compliance.
Every mutation must carry a valid subid registered in `deploy/config/subid-registry.json`.
Rejects mutations with unregistered or malformed subids. Maps `control_source`,
`control_refs`, and `statement_refs` to NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls.

**E.U.gene Risk (EU AI Act Counsel)** classifies AI system risk level. The
embedding pipeline (F) is "limited risk" under Article 50 (transparency
obligations). Requires documentation of which content was embedded and why.
The content-bearing subid gate — structural subids never embedded — satisfies
the auditability requirement. The battle-test plan (G) must produce a
transparency log per Article 12(1).

**Penny Privacy (GDPR Engine)** validates data minimization. Cozo relations
must not store PII (WireGuard-pubkey-keyed identities, not emails). Qdrant
embeddings of compliance corpora carry lawful basis Art 6(1)(f) legitimate
interest for system security/audit. Socket provisioning must not expose
personal data (WG-gated, UDS-only). `privacy_users` relation requires
explicit user directive for any PII storage. Right to erasure (Art 17)
applies to `memory_entries` and `mutation_audit` by namespace/actor key.

**Reggie O.P.A. (Cloud Prosecutor)** provides Open Policy Agent integration.
Evaluates the `compliance_rule` relation in cozo before every mutation:
`?[action, reason, control_ref] := *compliance_rule{plugin: $plugin, op: $op, action, reason, control_ref}`.
If `action == "Deny"`, the mutation is rejected, `audit_event` is written with
`verdict: "deny"`, and the caller receives the reason and control_ref.

### Compliance Gate Flow (per mutation)

1. Mutation arrives at `MutationEngine` with `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` and
   `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` headers injected by OpenClaw Trusted Proxy.
2. `SubidRouter` classifies the subid (or infers from plugin + member fields).
3. **Reggie O.P.A.** queries `compliance_rule` in cozo.
   — If `"Deny"`: mutation rejected; `audit_event` written with `verdict: "deny"`;
     caller receives reason + control_ref. Flow stops here.
   — If `"Allow"` (or no rule): flow continues.
4. **Olivia Scal** validates subid is registered in `subid_registry`.
5. **Penny Privacy** checks data minimization for the payload.
6. **E.U.gene Risk** classifies if content-bearing (for embedding gate).
7. Mutation written to `mutation_audit` and `audit_event` relations in cozo.
8. If content-bearing (`obs`/`exp` with non-empty text): embed via Voyage,
   upsert to qdrant.

### Accountability Loop (end-to-end)

1. User interacts via chatbot → `X-Ghostbridge-Footprint` (hashed WireGuard
   pubkey) + `X-Ghostbridge-Trace-ID` (session UUID) injected into gRPC
   metadata by OpenClaw Trusted Proxy.
2. `MutationEngine` receives mutation with footprint + trace_id.
3. `SubidRouter` classifies and routes to cozo (`mutation_audit` + `audit_event`)
   and optionally qdrant (embedding).
4. Cozo `audit_event`: `event_id => subid, plugin_id, operation, actor (footprint),
   verdict, reason, control_ref, timestamp`.
5. Cozo `mutation_audit`: `subid, uuid => timestamp, actor_id, capability_id,
   plugin_id, operation, old_json, new_json, footprint, trace_id, control_ref, verdict`.
6. Accountability page UI (`op-web`): chatbot actions on top, Qdrant semantic
   search on bottom.
7. User can search Qdrant for past actions by semantic query, confront chatbot
   with retrieved evidence.
8. Every `audit_event` is append-only (immutable), satisfying AU-6(a) review
   and AU-12 generation requirements.

- Seven categories: `src`, `prj`, `sch`, `mut`, `obs`, `evt`, `exp`
- Component-types: OSCAL vocabulary (`software`, `service`, `network`,
  `hardware`, `process-procedure`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`,

### FR-B1 — CozoPlugin reads state from shm projection; writes route through SubidRouter

`CozoPlugin` is a schema/state-shape declaration — it does NOT own an HTTP
client or a direct socket to cozoserver. The plugin follows the same model as
every other plugin:

- **Present-state reads** come from `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/cozo.json`

  shape; the D-Bus object exposes the current value.
- **Mutations** (writes to cozoserver relations) go through `MutationEngine` →
  broadcast → `SubidRouter`. The `SubidRouter` owns the connection to cozo
  — it reaches the container via the Ghostbridge socket

  direct HTTP call from inside the plugin.
- The embedded `/var/lib/opdbus/cognitive.db` path and `DEFAULT_COZO_DB_PATH`
  constant must be removed (they imply a direct embedded engine).

The `SubidRouter` issues the cozoserver HTTP API calls (`POST /api/mutate`
with Datalog scripts) over the gRPC-bridged path. No plugin file holds a
`reqwest::Client`.

NIST controls: AU-6, SC-8, SI-7

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `DEFAULT_COZO_DB_PATH` constant and any embedded `cozodb` engine import are
   absent from `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/cozo.rs`.

3. `CozoPlugin::schema()` declares the correct subids and calls

### FR-E3 — CozoDB relation schema for subid router audit trail

WHEN the subid router writes mutations,
THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain a `mutation_audit` relation in cozoserver with the
following schema:

```
:create mutation_audit {
    subid: String, uuid: String
    =>
    timestamp: String default "",
    actor_id: String default "",
    capability_id: String default "",
    plugin_id: String default "",
    operation: String default "",
    old_json: String default "{}",
    new_json: String default "{}",
    footprint: String default "",
    trace_id: String default "",
    control_ref: String default "",
    verdict: String default "allow"
}
```

Supporting relations the router reads/writes:
- `compliance_rule` — evaluated before every mutation (Reggie O.P.A.)
- `subid_registry` — canonical OSCAL subid entries (Olivia Scal validation)
- `audit_event` — append-only audit log (written for every mutation)
- `graph_node` / `graph_edge` — identity graph (for `src`, `prj`, `sch` subids)
- `memory_namespaces` / `memory_entries` — MCP memory (for `exp` subids)

Datalog write pattern:
```
?[subid, uuid, timestamp, actor_id, plugin_id, operation, new_json, footprint, trace_id]
<- $input_rows
:put mutation_audit { subid, uuid => timestamp, actor_id, plugin_id, operation, new_json, footprint, trace_id }
```

Compliance gate query (before every mutation):
```
?[action, reason, control_ref] :=
    *compliance_rule{plugin: $plugin, op: $op, action, reason, control_ref}
```

NIST controls: AU-2, AU-12 (via audit trail), AC-3 (via compliance gate)

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `mutation_audit` relation is created on first router write (`:create` is
   idempotent; "already exists" errors are ignored).
2. Every mutation that passes the compliance gate produces a row in `mutation_audit`.
3. Every denied mutation produces a row in `audit_event` with `verdict: "deny"`.
4. `cargo check -p op-grpc-bridge` passes.

`mut.software.rocksdb.set-option@v1` with `actor_id` + `capability_id` is the

change control).

#!/bin/sh
# check-subid-uniqueness.sh — CI gate for the canonical subid registry.
#
# Validates deploy/config/subid-registry.json:
#   1. every `uuid` is unique
#   2. every `subid` is unique
#   3. every entry that declares a non-empty `control_source` also carries at
#      least one `control_ref` and one `statement_ref` (NFR-13)
#
# Exits 0 on success, non-zero on any violation. Pure jq; no network, no build.

set -eu

REGISTRY="${1:-$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/../config" && pwd)/subid-registry.json}"

if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "check-subid-uniqueness: jq is required" >&2
    exit 2
fi

if [ ! -f "$REGISTRY" ]; then
    echo "check-subid-uniqueness: registry not found: $REGISTRY" >&2
    exit 2
fi

status=0

uuid_dupes=$(jq -r '[.entries[].uuid] | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1) | .[0]) | .[]' "$REGISTRY")
if [ -n "$uuid_dupes" ]; then
    echo "DUPLICATE uuid(s):" >&2
    echo "$uuid_dupes" >&2
    status=1
fi

subid_dupes=$(jq -r '[.entries[].subid] | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1) | .[0]) | .[]' "$REGISTRY")
if [ -n "$subid_dupes" ]; then
    echo "DUPLICATE subid(s):" >&2
    echo "$subid_dupes" >&2
    status=1
fi

# NFR-13: entries with a control_source must carry control_refs + statement_refs.
empty_mappings=$(jq -r '
    .entries[]
    | select((.control_source // "") != "")
    | select(((.control_refs // []) | length) == 0 or ((.statement_refs // []) | length) == 0)
    | .subid' "$REGISTRY")
if [ -n "$empty_mappings" ]; then
    echo "INCOMPLETE NIST mappings (control_source set but missing control_refs/statement_refs):" >&2
    echo "$empty_mappings" >&2
    status=1
fi

if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
    count=$(jq -r '.entries | length' "$REGISTRY")
    echo "check-subid-uniqueness: OK ($count entries, uuids+subids unique)"
fi

exit "$status"
